fullPassage:
【Story 1】The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports. One day, there is a table-tennis table in the garage as a surprise from his parents. The boy challenges his dad to a match.

The boy faces a big choice: challenge himself with endurance and courage, or avoid difficulties.

[Path of Avoidance] He misses the ball, bruises his elbow, and gives up. He refuses to play the next week and turns down his mom's suggestion to play his brother. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are obstacles—best avoided.

[Path of Embracing Challenge] He picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still wins easily, but the boy is learning. He challenges his brother too. He practices until he joins the regional team—reaching the national finals. He sneaks the ball past his opponent at match point. He has become truly awesome!

This is the story of Matthew Syed, a former British national table-tennis team member. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried new things, discovered his passion, and became tough facing difficult tasks. You, too, can find your own "table tennis." Embrace the challenge and never give up.

【Story 2】Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Being a real teenager presents its own challenges. Resilience is the ability to adapt to challenging experiences. Humans can recover from hardship—and you can develop this skill. Resilience will not prevent problems, but helps you face them.

Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. Resilience means: you experience, feel, fail, hurt, and fall—but you keep going. It takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage:
【Story 1】The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports. One day, there is a table-tennis table in the garage as a surprise from his parents. The boy challenges his dad to a match.

The boy faces a big choice: challenge himself with endurance and courage, or avoid difficulties.

[Path of Avoidance] He misses the ball, bruises his elbow, and gives up. He refuses to play the next week and turns down his mom's suggestion to play his brother. "He's going to be better than me anyway." In his eyes, challenges are obstacles—best avoided.

[Path of Embracing Challenge] He picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still wins easily, but the boy is learning. He challenges his brother too. He practices until he joins the regional team—reaching the national finals. He sneaks the ball past his opponent at match point. He has become truly awesome!

This is the story of Matthew Syed, a former British national table-tennis team member. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried new things, discovered his passion, and became tough facing difficult tasks. You, too, can find your own "table tennis." Embrace the challenge and never give up.

【Story 2】Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Being a real teenager presents its own challenges. Resilience is the ability to adapt to challenging experiences. Humans can recover from hardship—and you can develop this skill. Resilience will not prevent problems, but helps you face them.

Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. Resilience means: you experience, feel, fail, hurt, and fall—but you keep going. It takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.
